newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Peacekeepers in Liberia seal Sierra Leone border.
newsitem.headline: Peacekeepers in Liberia seal Sierra Leone border.

text.p: The ECOMOG African peacekeeping force in Liberia said on Monday its troops had sealed the land frontier with Sierra Leone and that naval units were patrolling coastal waters after the coup in Freetown.

Port officials and military sources in Monrovia said two naval boats left with hundreds of battle-ready ECOMOG troops on Sunday night, presumably heading for Sierra Leone. ECOMOG troops in Freetown were drawn into battle with coup soldiers on Sunday.

ECOMOG deputy force commander Brigadier-General Joe Kwateng told reporters in Monrovia that peacekeeping soldiers deployed in Liberia's western Grand Cape Mount country had been ordered to seal the Sierra Leone border.
"As part of the operation, soldiers of ECOMOG's navy battalion are continuing their patrol of international waters and have also stepped up border patrol," Kwateng said.
He declined to comment on the departure of boatloads of ECOMOG soldiers, but said: "The situation in Sierra Leone is an internal matter, but our men are there going about their assigned duties."

The military seized power in Sierra Leone on Sunday. The coup leaders said they wanted to bring rebels of the Revolutionary United Front into the government to consolidate an elusive peace in the country's civil war.
